meta.subtitle: Streamlined two-segment specialty maker after the Qnity spin-off and Aramids sale; Q2'26 continuing-ops sales up 4% and full-year guidance raised

analystSentiment.commentary: We rate DuPont BUY with a target range of $150 to $180. The case rests on a simpler company: after spinning off its Electronics Business into Qnity Electronics on November 1, 2025 and selling its Aramids business on April 1, 2026, DuPont now reports two continuing segments — Healthcare & Water Technologies and Diversified Industrials — with both transactions carried as discontinued operations and comparative periods restated. Second-quarter 2026 net sales were $1,819 million, {+ up 4% +} from $1,749 million, all of it organic. GAAP income from continuing operations was $191 million and operating EBITDA was $448 million, a 24.6% operating EBITDA margin. Adjusted EPS was $1.88, {+ up 48% +} from $1.27. Management raised full-year 2026 guidance, lifting the operating EBITDA midpoint to approximately $1.76 billion and adjusted EPS to $7.24. Reported trailing earnings are depressed by separation and one-time charges, so we anchor on the forward view, where consensus targets $170.00 against the $130.88 price. The main risks are cyclicality in Diversified Industrials, unresolved tax and PFAS liabilities from the prior separations, and execution on the standalone cost base.

executiveSummary.companyOverview: DuPont de Nemours, Inc. provides technology-based materials and solutions across healthcare, water, construction and industrial markets. Following a run of portfolio actions it now operates through two segments: Healthcare & Water Technologies and Diversified Industrials. Healthcare & Water Technologies supplies specialty components for medical devices, packaging and protective garments under the TYVEK brand, plus water filtration and separation products including AMBERLITE ion exchange resins, FILMTEC reverse osmosis and nanofiltration elements, and INGE and ITEGRATEC ultrafiltration modules. Diversified Industrials spans engineered products for construction — TYVEK house wrap, STYROFOAM insulation and CORIAN solid surface — and engineered components and process solutions for automotive, aerospace, printing and packaging, including Vespel shapes and parts, MOLYKOTE specialty lubricants, BETAFORCE and BETASEAL structural adhesives, and Cyrel flexographic printing plates. The company was incorporated in 2015, is headquartered in Wilmington, Delaware, was formerly known as DowDuPont Inc. and took the DuPont de Nemours name in June 2019. Today's DuPont is materially smaller than the group that reported $12.6 billion of revenue in FY21: the Mobility & Materials business was divested, the Electronics Business was spun off as Qnity Electronics on November 1, 2025, and the Aramids business was sold on April 1, 2026, with the latter two now carried as discontinued operations and prior periods restated. Its GICS classification changed to Industrials effective July 31, 2026.

thesis.label: BUY
thesis.body: The thesis is that a smaller, two-segment DuPont converts steady mid-single-digit organic growth into margin expansion and free cash flow, and that the shares re-rate as the separation overhang clears. Second-quarter 2026 net sales rose 4% to $1,819 million, with operating EBITDA of $448 million and a 24.6% operating EBITDA margin, {+ up 40 bps +} year on year. Management raised full-year 2026 guidance, taking the operating EBITDA midpoint to about $1.76 billion and adjusted EPS to $7.24, and guided organic sales growth to a mid-single-digit pace. With reported trailing earnings held down by the separations and one-time items, valuation is better read on forward estimates, where consensus targets $170.00 against a $130.88 price. The counter-case is that Diversified Industrials is exposed to construction and industrial cycles, and that tax and PFAS liabilities from prior separations remain open.

catalysts: Execution against raised full-year 2026 guidance — net sales of $7,160 to $7,190 million and operating EBITDA of $1,750 to $1,770 million — is the near-term catalyst.
A $250 million share repurchase is planned for the third quarter under the $2 billion buyback authorized on November 6, 2025.

Transaction-adjusted free cash flow reached $326 million in the quarter, a 127% conversion, and cash from operating activities on continuing operations was $400 million, pointing to improving cash generation.
Interest expense fell to $41 million from $84 million as the capital structure was reset after the Electronics Separation, aiding continuing-operations earnings.
A re-rating toward the consensus target as separation and one-time charges roll off trailing results and the market values the simplified company on forward earnings.
risks: Diversified Industrials sells into construction, automotive, aerospace and printing end-markets; a downturn in non-residential construction or industrial demand would pressure its organic growth and 22.1% operating EBITDA margin.

Tax liabilities from the Qnity Distribution, the M&M Divestitures and the Nutrition & Biosciences transaction remain contingent; a failure to qualify for non-recognition treatment could impose significant tax on DuPont.
PFAS and PFOA liabilities are shared among DuPont, Corteva and The Chemours Company, and litigation outcomes are uncertain.
Reported GAAP earnings still carry separation and one-time charges, so a slower-than-expected normalization could weigh on sentiment until the run-rate is visible.
Guidance assumes continued mid-single-digit organic sales growth; a shortfall would challenge the raised operating EBITDA and adjusted EPS targets.

income.note: Source: Bigdata.com company tearsheet (FMP); fiscal years ended December 31.

financials.incomeCommentary: On continuing operations, second-quarter 2026 net sales were $1,819 million, up 4% from $1,749 million a year earlier, all of the gain organic; over the six months to June 30 net sales were $3,500 million versus $3,361 million. Cost of sales held at 65% of net sales. Operating EBITDA, the measure management uses for segment profit, was $448 million at a 24.6% margin, up 40 basis points year on year, and GAAP income from continuing operations was $191 million, up from $24 million. GAAP EPS from continuing operations was $1.37 and adjusted EPS was $1.88, up 48% from $1.27. Three items flattered the year-on-year comparison: interest expense fell to $41 million from $84 million after the post-separation capital-structure reset, acquisition, integration and separation costs dropped to $7 million from $55 million, and the effective tax rate on continuing operations was 28.2% versus 69.2% a year earlier when transaction items dominated. A word on the multi-year series: the annual revenue line — $12.6 billion in FY21 and $13.0 billion in FY22, then $6.6 billion in FY23 and $6.8 billion in FY25 — reflects successive, larger portfolios and repeated separations, so it is not continuous with today's two-segment continuing operations; the reported FY25 net loss of $779 million and diluted EPS of -$1.86 sit inside that transition. Read the quarter against the prior-year quarter, not against a full historical year. Consensus sees FY26E revenue of $7.2 billion and EPS of $7.26, rising to $7.4 billion and $7.96 in FY27E.

balance.note: Source: Bigdata.com company tearsheet (FMP); fiscal years ended December 31.

financials.balanceCommentary: The balance sheet is unusually clean for a chemicals company after the deleveraging that accompanied the separations. As of June 30, 2026 DuPont held approximately $1.7 billion in cash and cash equivalents and $2.9 billion of working capital. At FY25 year-end the vendor data show cash and short-term investments of $0.7 billion, total debt of $60 million and net debt of -$655 million — a net cash position — with total equity of $14.1 billion and net debt to EBITDA of -1.6x on a trailing basis. The current ratio was 2.42. The Aramids Divestiture on April 1, 2026 added pre-tax cash proceeds of approximately $1.2 billion plus a $300 million note receivable and a $325 million equity interest in Arclin, further supporting liquidity. Management expects cash on hand, operating cash flow and access to debt markets to cover the liquidity needs of continuing operations. The equity base stepped down from $23.8 billion at FY24 as the Electronics Business was distributed to shareholders.

cashflow.note: Source: Bigdata.com company tearsheet (FMP); fiscal years ended December 31.

financials.cashflowCommentary: Cash generation improved on continuing operations. In the second quarter, cash provided by operating activities from continuing operations was $400 million, up from $74 million a year earlier, and transaction-adjusted free cash flow was $326 million, a conversion of 127%; capital expenditures in the quarter were $76 million. Historically the vendor series shows FY25 operating cash flow of $0.6 billion, capital expenditure of -$333 million and free cash flow of $227 million, a 3.3% FCF margin, with a trailing FCF yield of 4.0%. Dividends remain a fixture: the Board declared second- and third-quarter 2026 dividends of $0.60 per share each, retrospectively adjusted for the 1-for-3 reverse stock split effective June 24, 2026, and FY25 dividends paid were $597 million. The stock yields 1.83%.

multiples.note: Peer multiples pending a peer data source.

valuation.multiplesCommentary: Trailing multiples are not usable here. The reported P/E of 233.7x and trailing net margin of 0.8% are distorted by separation costs and one-time charges running through continuing operations, and the FY25 net loss of $779 million makes the earnings base unrepresentative. EV/EBITDA of 14.5x and price-to-sales of 2.5x are steadier, and the more relevant lens is forward: the stock trades at 18.0x next-twelve-months earnings and about 16.4x FY27E EPS of $7.96, against consensus FY26E EPS of $7.26. On those forward earnings the $130.88 price is not demanding for a business guiding to mid-single-digit organic growth and rising operating EBITDA. The Street is constructive: 17 analysts split 14 Buy, 3 Hold and 0 Sell, with a consensus target of $170.00 (+29.9%), a median of $171.00 and a range of $156.00 to $186.00.

scenarios.name: Bull
scenarios.driver: DuPont sustains organic growth slightly above 4% with further operating EBITDA margin expansion, executes the $250 million third-quarter buyback and more of the $2 billion authorization, and the market re-rates the simplified two-segment company toward $186.00 as separation charges clear.

scenarios.name: Base
scenarios.driver: Organic growth holds in the mid-single digits and DuPont meets its raised FY26 guidance of about $1.76 billion operating EBITDA and $7.24 adjusted EPS; the shares track toward the lower half of the analyst target range, near our $165 Base, as the market values continuing operations on forward earnings.

scenarios.name: Bear
scenarios.driver: Industrial and construction demand in Diversified Industrials softens, organic growth stalls, and an adverse tax or PFAS outcome from the prior separations weighs on earnings and the multiple; the shares fall toward $110.

valuation.scenarioCommentary: We weight the Base case at 45%, the Bull at 25% and the Bear at 30%. The Base assumes DuPont delivers its raised 2026 guidance and grows organically in the mid-single digits, supporting a valuation in the lower half of the Street's target range; our Base implied price is $165. The Bull, at $186, sits at the top of that range and assumes margin expansion continues and the buyback shrinks the share count. The Bear, at $110, is a genuine downside: it reflects a cyclical stall in Diversified Industrials and an adverse tax or PFAS development, and sits well below the current price. On these probabilities the reward outweighs the downside, which supports a BUY rating and a $150 to $180 target range that brackets the Base case. The chief uncertainty is not near-term demand, which held up across the business in the quarter, but the tail liabilities from the separations, which are hard to size from the disclosures.

segments.name: Consolidated
segments.body: DuPont reports a single consolidated result made up of two continuing segments. Consolidated second-quarter 2026 net sales were $1,819 million, up 4% from $1,749 million, with group operating EBITDA of $448 million at a 24.6% margin. Healthcare & Water Technologies contributed net sales of $856 million (up 5% from $817 million) and operating EBITDA of $258 million at a 30.1% margin, selling TYVEK medical and protective materials plus AMBERLITE, FILMTEC and INGE water-separation products into medical, biopharma, industrial water and semiconductor markets. Diversified Industrials contributed net sales of $963 million (up 3% from $932 million) and operating EBITDA of $213 million at a 22.1% margin, spanning TYVEK house wrap, STYROFOAM and CORIAN construction products and engineered components such as Vespel, MOLYKOTE and Cyrel for automotive, aerospace and printing markets.

moatFactors.name: Specialty brands and formulations
moatFactors.body: DuPont sells branded, specified materials — TYVEK, STYROFOAM, CORIAN, Vespel, MOLYKOTE, AMBERLITE and FILMTEC — that are often written into customer specifications and regulatory approvals in medical, water and construction applications. That specification lock-in supports pricing power in the Healthcare & Water Technologies franchise.

moatFactors.name: Water separation technology
moatFactors.body: The water franchise combines reverse osmosis (FILMTEC), ultrafiltration (INGE, ITEGRATEC) and ion exchange (AMBERLITE) across industrial, municipal, desalination and life-sciences uses. Management cited continued strength in industrial water and semiconductor markets, indicating durable demand for separation technology.

moatFactors.name: Diversified end-markets
moatFactors.body: Continuing operations span healthcare, water, construction, automotive, aerospace and printing, so no single cycle dominates; that diversification cushions the group against a downturn in any one market and showed through in the quarter's broad-based growth.

moatFactors.name: Balance-sheet strength
moatFactors.body: After the separations DuPont carries total debt of $60 million and a net cash position of -$655 million net debt at FY25, with net debt to EBITDA of -1.6x. That gives the company flexibility to invest, return cash and absorb contingent liabilities without balance-sheet stress.

businessMoat.durability: Durability rests on specification-driven positions and a strong balance sheet rather than scale. The branded materials and water-separation technologies are embedded in customer designs and regulatory approvals, which slows switching, and the FY25 net cash position gives DuPont room to fund research and capital return through a cycle. The main threats to durability are cyclicality in Diversified Industrials' construction and industrial markets and the contingent tax and PFAS liabilities carried over from the Electronics, Mobility & Materials and Nutrition & Biosciences separations. The moat also depends on sustained research investment, because those specified positions erode if the product pipeline stalls. On balance the moat is narrow — real but not impregnable — and depends on that reinvestment and a clean resolution of the legacy liabilities.

points: Both continuing segments grew organically in the second quarter of 2026 — Healthcare & Water Technologies up 4% and Diversified Industrials up 3%.
Management raised full-year 2026 guidance to net sales of $7,160 to $7,190 million and operating EBITDA of $1,750 to $1,770 million, and lifted its organic sales growth outlook.
Consensus models revenue growth from $7.2 billion in FY26E to $7.4 billion in FY27E, with EPS rising from $7.26 to $7.96.

Growth drivers cited include personal protection and biopharma in healthcare, industrial water and semiconductor demand in water, and aerospace and electric-vehicle applications in Industrial Technologies.
The reset post-separation cost base — lower amortization of intangibles at $68 million versus $74 million and reduced separation costs — supports operating leverage as sales grow.

The bullish read has a counter-case: research and development spend fell to $42 million in the quarter from $53 million a year earlier, and a lighter innovation budget could slow the new-product cadence that underpins the demand drivers above.

management.leadership: Lori Koch is Chief Executive Officer and Antonella Franzen is Chief Financial Officer; both are quoted in the second-quarter 2026 results. Koch framed the quarter as mid-single-digit organic growth with margin expansion and strong free cash flow, and Franzen detailed the raised full-year guidance. Mr. Breen, the former CEO who led the Company's strategic transformation, continues as non-executive Chairman of the Board. The team has executed a sequence of complex separations — the Electronics spin into Qnity and the Aramids sale — while keeping the continuing business growing, which is evidence of operational control.
management.capitalAllocation: Capital allocation is balanced across the balance sheet, dividends and buybacks. DuPont declared second- and third-quarter 2026 dividends of $0.60 per share each, and the stock yields 1.83%. It announced a $250 million share repurchase for the third quarter under the $2 billion authorization from November 6, 2025. The Aramids Divestiture brought in approximately $1.2 billion of pre-tax cash plus a $300 million note and a $325 million equity stake, and the post-separation balance sheet carries net cash, so the company can sustain returns while investing. Capital expenditure was modest at $76 million in the quarter, consistent with an asset-light specialty model.
management.governance: Governance rests on the 2026 proxy statement. The Board has determined that all directors other than Mr. Breen and Ms. Koch are independent, a substantial majority, and that all members of the Audit, People and Compensation, and Nomination and Governance Committees are independent under NYSE standards. The Board separates the Chair and CEO roles, with Mr. Breen as non-executive Chairman and Ms. Koch as CEO. Related-person transactions are reviewed and approved or ratified by the Nomination and Governance Committee, with no director permitted to participate in a matter involving a family member. The disclosures describe standard, shareholder-aligned governance; the pack does not include detail on executive pay levels.
management.insiderOwnership: The pack does not include an insider-ownership table or beneficial-ownership percentages, so we do not quantify insider holdings here. The proxy confirms only that Mr. Breen and Ms. Koch are the non-independent directors, consistent with their executive and former-executive roles.

idiosyncratic: Contingent tax liabilities: if the Qnity Distribution or related transactions fail to qualify for non-recognition treatment, DuPont could face significant tax liability, allocated between DuPont and Qnity under the Electronics Tax Matters Agreement. Similar exposure exists for the M&M Divestitures and the Nutrition & Biosciences separation with IFF.

PFAS and PFOA liabilities are shared among DuPont, Corteva and The Chemours Company; the extent and cost of remediation and litigation, including personal-injury and natural-resource-damage claims, are uncertain and could be material.

Cyclical demand: Diversified Industrials depends on construction, automotive, aerospace and printing markets. A downturn would pressure the segment's organic growth and its 22.1% operating EBITDA margin.

Execution on separation benefits: DuPont must realize the intended synergies and cost savings from the Electronics Separation and Aramids Divestiture; failure to do so, or disputes over separated liabilities, would hurt continuing results.

Part of the Aramids sale proceeds is non-cash: a $300 million note receivable and a $325 million equity interest in Arclin. The realizable value of that consideration depends on Arclin's performance rather than DuPont's, a genuine exposure separate from the operating business.
risks.systemic: Systemic risks are macro and geopolitical. Management flagged that in February 2026 military conflict in the Middle East involving the United States, Israel and Iran heightened geopolitical uncertainty; DuPont has no operations in Iran and reports no material impact to date, but disruption to global logistics and supply chains is a risk. Separately, in February 2026 the U.S. Supreme Court invalidated certain tariffs imposed under the International Emergency Economic Powers Act; DuPont has begun receiving refunds, shares 44 percent of pre-November 1, 2025 tariff refunds with Qnity, and notes the ruling remains subject to appeal. Broader exposure to raw-material, energy and logistics costs, currency swings — the U.S. dollar weakened against the Euro in the period — and trade or tariff actions affecting exports to China round out the systemic set.

body: Our recommendation is BUY, with a fair-value range of $150 to $180. The case is a cleaner, two-segment company that grew organic sales 4% in the second quarter of 2026, expanded its operating EBITDA margin to 24.6%, and raised full-year guidance to about $1.76 billion of operating EBITDA and $7.24 of adjusted EPS. We look past the reported 233.7x trailing P/E, which is skewed by separation charges, to the forward view: the $130.88 price sits at 18.0x next-twelve-months earnings against a $170.00 consensus target.

The risks are real: contingent tax liabilities and shared PFAS exposure from the prior separations, and cyclicality in Diversified Industrials. Our Bear case at $110 reflects those, and we weight it at 30%. Even so, the probability-weighted setup favors upside, and the net cash balance sheet — total debt of $60 million and a -$655 million net debt position — gives management room to fund the dividend, the planned $250 million buyback and reinvestment while the legacy liabilities resolve.
